trust_decision.summary: Whether a stored in-app notification redirect URL (message cta.data.url and primary/secondary button url, plus target), which can come from subscriber-controlled trigger payload through template compilation, is a safe scheme (http/https, single-slash relative path, template var) before the Inbox opens it. At the pinned commit nobody decides this when the message is delivered: the API mapper, both websocket mappers and the client navigate() all pass it through as-is.

landing_point.why: The summary says the Inbox follows a redirect.url with a javascript: scheme. navigate() is the single function that calls window.open(url, target) for every notification and action click (packages/js/src/ui/components/Notification/DefaultNotification.tsx:103,113,118).

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/js/src/ws/party-socket.ts:99-123 and packages/js/src/ws/socket.ts:94-118 (realtime mappers that build Notification.redirect from the raw message, separate from the API mapper apps/api/src/app/inbox/utils/notification-mapper.ts:62-90)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once the API mapper sanitizes, websocket payloads look like they come from Novu's own trusted server, and the socket.io socket looks like a legacy transport next to PartySocket, so a solver could argue that client-side sanitization in the socket mappers is just redundant defence in depth.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: These must keep working: template-variable URLs ({{payload.x}}, https://x/{{id}}), single-slash relative paths sent through the host app's routerPush/pushState, http(s) with any of the five window targets, and an invalid target must drop only the target, not the URL. A scheme allowlist that rejects {{...}} or relative paths, or that drops the whole redirect when the target is bad, breaks legitimate notifications.
